comparables.description: FPI's own 2025 dispositions: 60 properties for $90.2M aggregate consideration; net gain $34.9M implies sales above book

methodology:
FPI's 121 Schedule III line items are mapped to 10 valuation clusters by state and ground quality. Each property carries an explicit per-acre FMV backed by 2-5 cited comparables — all dated within the last 24 months (cutoff May 2024). The "FMV by category" table at top is fully derived from this per-property analysis.

Primary comp sources, all 2024-2025 dated:
- USDA NASS 2025 Land Values Summary (published August 2025) for state-average cropland anchors
- Iowa State CARD 2024 + 2025 Land Value Surveys for Class-A Midwest premium benchmarks
- Illinois Society of Professional Farm Managers 2024 + 2025 Land Values Conference for Class-A vs. Class-B Illinois ground
- Recent Q4 2024 / Q1 2025 farmland auction reports (Hertz, Sullivan, Murray Wise)
- State-specific industry reports (LSU AgCenter, Texas A&M AgriLife, UNL, Clemson Extension, Mizzou Extension)
- FPI's own FY2025 disposition pricing ($7,100/acre weighted across 60 properties / $90.2M) as the residual aggregate benchmark

Illinois Class-A is the cluster that drives most of the FMV picture — properties encumbered by MetLife loans (footnotes c/e/f/g/h/i/j) sit on tier-1 central-Illinois ground that ISPFMRA 2025 prices at $14,500/acre. The FMV/acre of $13,500 used here weights that benchmark slightly down for portfolio mix and consistency with 2025 auction comps. The 60-farm "Other" aggregate is conservatively marked at FPI's actual 2025 sale price, which is the most defensible reference point for that residual.

The implied NAV/share at FMV deducts net debt (debt + Series A pref RNCI − cash) and divides by 43.1M diluted shares. The premium-to-book is structurally tighter than LAND because Midwest row-crop tracks closer to USDA-published state averages than California permanent crops do.

PER-PROPERTY CAP RATES (latest pass): Each FPI property now carries a
cap rate range matched to its cluster (Illinois Class-A 3.0-4.0%,
Texas dryland 6.0-8.5%, etc.). The NOI cross-check FMV-weighted-averages
these across the portfolio to derive a defensible issuer-level
benchmark, replacing the prior keyword-based "US row-crop 3.5-4.5%"
single range. The mix-weighted result better reflects FPI's actual
geographic footprint (which spans tier-1 Class-A through Texas High
Plains dryland).
